bookTitle: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets

facts.statement: Flags and pennants represent brief consolidation pauses within a dynamic, steep market move, allowing an overextended trend to catch its breath before continuation.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Continuation Patterns: Flags, Pennants, Wedges & Rectangles

facts.statement: These continuation formations require heavy trading volume during the initial flagpole surge, a significant drop in volume during pattern consolidation, and an abrupt expansion of volume upon breakout.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Continuation Patterns: Flags, Pennants, Wedges & Rectangles
sourceCitation.excerpt: drying up of volume while the pattern forms...

facts.statement: The vertical height of the flagpole is determined by calculating the absolute difference between the extreme price peak of the flagpole and the initial breakout level.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Continuation Patterns: Flags, Pennants, Wedges & Rectangles

variables.definition: Peak price level of the flagpole

facts.statement: Price projections for flags and pennants apply the half-mast principle by adding or subtracting the flagpole height from the breakout point.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Continuation Patterns: Flags, Pennants, Wedges & Rectangles

variables.definition: Breakout price from the flag or pennant pattern

facts.statement: Wedges are intermediate consolidation patterns defined by converging trendlines; falling wedges slope downward against uptrends and are bullish, whereas rising wedges slope upward against downtrends and are bearish.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Continuation Patterns: Flags, Pennants, Wedges & Rectangles
sourceCitation.excerpt: falling wedge is bullish... rising wedge is bearish

facts.statement: The base height of a wedge pattern is calculated by measuring the absolute price spread at its widest part near the beginning of formation.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Continuation Patterns: Flags, Pennants, Wedges & Rectangles

variables.definition: Base height of the wedge pattern
Highest price boundary at the base
Lowest price boundary at the base

facts.statement: Rectangles are sideways consolidation pauses bound by parallel horizontal support and resistance lines reflecting lateral price congestion over intermediate time horizons.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Continuation Patterns: Flags, Pennants, Wedges & Rectangles
sourceCitation.excerpt: sideways consolidation pauses where price moves laterally

facts.statement: The height of a rectangle trading range is the vertical distance between its horizontal resistance and support boundaries, used to project post-breakout targets.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Continuation Patterns: Flags, Pennants, Wedges & Rectangles

facts.statement: In a measured move sequence, the countertrend corrective wave typically retraces between one-third and one-half of the initial trend leg before initiating the second parallel advance or decline.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Continuation Patterns: Flags, Pennants, Wedges & Rectangles
sourceCitation.excerpt: retraces 33% to 50% (1/3 to 1/2) of wave AB

facts.statement: The price target for a measured move is calculated by adding or subtracting the vertical height of the first trend leg from the extreme price point of the corrective retracement.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Continuation Patterns: Flags, Pennants, Wedges & Rectangles

variables.definition: Final projected target price point D
Correction low or high point C
End point of first trend leg B
Start point of first trend leg A

facts.topic: Procter & Gamble Measured Move Case Study
facts.statement: Procter & Gamble daily chart demonstrated a 20-point initial upleg from point A to B followed by a correction down to 62 at point C, yielding an exact projected target of 82.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Continuation Patterns: Flags, Pennants, Wedges & Rectangles
sourceCitation.excerpt: Procter & Gamble Co. (PG) daily bar chart: Prior upleg AB measured 20 points... yielding an exact measured price target of D = 82

facts.statement: Unlike flags or wedges where volume contracts sharply during pattern formation, rectangle trading ranges maintain active trading volume across their wide price swings.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Continuation Patterns: Flags, Pennants, Wedges & Rectangles
sourceCitation.excerpt: wide price swings inside a rectangle maintain trading activity

facts.topic: Support and Resistance Role Reversal in Rectangles
facts.statement: Upon a decisive breakout from a rectangular trading range, the former resistance ceiling acts as a new support floor on pullbacks, and vice versa for downside breakdowns.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Continuation Patterns: Flags, Pennants, Wedges & Rectangles
sourceCitation.excerpt: former resistance ceiling becomes a support floor on pullbacks

facts.statement: Continuation patterns such as flags, pennants, and wedges reflect temporary market pauses that almost invariably resolve in the direction of cemeteries or prevailing primary trends.

sourceCitation.book: Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets
sourceCitation.chapter: Continuation Patterns: Flags, Pennants, Wedges & Rectangles
sourceCitation.excerpt: highly reliable continuation patterns and rarely result in trend reversals

generalAssumptions: Market action discounts all known and unknown fundamentals.
Prices move in trends, and a trend in motion is more likely to continue than to reverse.
